name: Scandinavian interior photography
summary: Calm, bright pictures of rooms: pale wood, white walls, a window and a few objects. The light is soft, the lines are straight and the space is allowed to breathe.

philosophy.core_thesis: A room looks livable when the light is honest and the objects are few, so the picture shows the light first.
design_principles: Shoot with a tilt-shift or a 24mm to 35mm lens at f/8 to f/11, with the camera level at 1.0m to 1.2m high.
Use window light only: turn off lamps, and add a white 1.2m reflector on the shadow side.
Keep a key-to-fill ratio of 2:1 to 3:1, so that shadows stay soft and open.
Correct all verticals to 0° and hold the horizon at 0°.
Set 3 to 5 objects in the room; leave 40–60% of the frame as wall, floor or air.
Grade to cool daylight, 5500–6000K, and a low saturation of −10 to −20% in a palette of white, pale wood and one green.
anti_patterns: Overhead lamps, flash or mixed colour casts
Converging verticals from a tilted camera

composition.framing: Square-on or a soft corner view; the room reads as a calm box.
composition.viewpoint: Level at 1.0m to 1.2m high, 3 to 6m from the far wall.
composition.geometry: Horizontal planes and vertical edges; a window and a table form a quiet grid.
composition.subject_placement: Centred on a wall or off-centre on a third, with 40–60% as open space.

principles.rule: Leave 40–60% of the frame as wall, floor or air.
Hold a visual weight ratio of 0.8–1.25 between the window side and the furniture side.
Set the main object within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.
Use 2 layers: window key and a white bounce at 1 stop under it.
Set 70% in white and pale wood, 20% in grey-blue and 10% in one green accent.

light.quality: Soft and even window daylight with a white bounce.
light.direction: From the side window at 90° to the lens; a reflector fills the opposite side.
light.time_of_day: Overcast morning, or midday with a diffuser at the window

lens_and_camera.format: Digital full frame or medium format; tilt-shift lens for vertical control
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus one third into the room; the depth of field covers 1m to infinity.
lens_and_camera.support: Tripod, with a level on the hot shoe

colour_and_grade.treatment: Soft, cool daylight colour with lowered saturation and open shadows.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 5800K, tint 0.
Raise shadows by +25 and lower highlights by −20.
Reduce saturation by −12% and warm tones by −5%.
Add +10% clarity on wood grain only.
Correct verticals to 0° and horizon to 0°.
Add no grain and no vignette.
colour_and_grade.grain: None: clean, with a low noise floor at ISO 100

subject_and_staging.staging: Styled: remove clutter, set 3 to 5 objects, add a plant, a throw and a ceramic; steam the linen.
subject_and_staging.direction: Check every line in live view; adjust objects in steps of 2cm.

workflow: Shoot a 3-frame bracket at ±1 stop for window detail.
Blend by hand for windows; no automatic HDR.
Export at 4:5 or 3:2 sRGB, 2400px on the long edge.
post_processing.output: A bright, quiet room image for a magazine page, a brand site or a catalogue.

emotion.target_response: Calm and comfort: the viewer feels able to breathe and live in the room.

use_cases: property marketing with a calm look
avoid_when: The brief needs drama, deep colour or night mood.
The room is cluttered and must stay as it is.

modifiers.how: Add a large soft box at 4:1 from the window side, use a coloured sweep and place a model in the room at f/5.6.
Remove all soft styling, use f/32 on a view camera, and show the room as a frontal plate in black and white.

sources.title: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Interior with Young Woman from Behind (1904)
Julius Shulman, Photographing Architecture and Interiors (Whitney Library of Design, 1962)
